questions.q:
State the output of each statement:
(a) OUTPUT LENGTH("Revision") [1]
(b) OUTPUT UCASE(SUBSTRING("Revision", 3, 4)) [1]
ms: (b) VISI
questions.model:
(a) 8
(b) SUBSTRING("Revision", 3, 4) starts at the 3rd character and takes 4 characters: "visi". UCASE gives VISI.
questions.tip: In Cambridge pseudocode the first character is position 1.

questions.q: Explain what is meant by a constant and give one reason for using a constant instead of a variable.
ms: a named value that cannot change while the program runs (1)
reason: value only needs changing in one place / easier to maintain (1); or prevents accidental change / makes the program easier to read (1)
questions.model: A constant is a named data item whose value is set once and cannot change while the program is running, for example CONSTANT VATRate ← 0.2. Using a constant means that if the value ever has to change, it only needs updating in one place.

questions.q:
Write a function in pseudocode called CountVowels that takes a string as a parameter and returns the number of vowels (a, e, i, o, u, in upper or lower case) in the string.
Then write a statement that uses the function to output the number of vowels in "Computer".
ms: function header with a STRING parameter and RETURNS INTEGER, and ENDFUNCTION (1)
initialises a counter to 0 (1)
loop from 1 to LENGTH of the string (1)
extracts each character with SUBSTRING and checks it against all vowels, handling case (e.g. LCASE) (1)
increments counter and RETURNs it after the loop (1)
calling statement, e.g. OUTPUT CountVowels("Computer") (1)
questions.model:
FUNCTION CountVowels(Word : STRING) RETURNS INTEGER
   DECLARE Count : INTEGER
   DECLARE Letter : STRING
   Count ← 0
   FOR Position ← 1 TO LENGTH(Word)
      Letter ← LCASE(SUBSTRING(Word, Position, 1))
      IF Letter = "a" OR Letter = "e" OR Letter = "i" OR Letter = "o" OR Letter = "u"
         THEN
            Count ← Count + 1
      ENDIF
   NEXT Position
   RETURN Count
ENDFUNCTION

OUTPUT CountVowels("Computer")   // outputs 3
questions.tip: A function must RETURN a value; a procedure does not.

questions.q:
Write a procedure Stars that takes an integer N as a parameter and outputs a line of N asterisks (*).
Then write pseudocode that calls the procedure to output this pattern:
*
**
***
****
*****
ms: procedure header with an INTEGER parameter, and ENDPROCEDURE (1)
builds the line using a loop from 1 to N and concatenation (&), or outputs N asterisks on one line (1)
outputs the line (once, after the loop) (1)
loop from 1 to 5 that CALLs Stars with the loop counter (1)
questions.model:
PROCEDURE Stars(N : INTEGER)
   DECLARE Line : STRING
   Line ← ""
   FOR Count ← 1 TO N
      Line ← Line & "*"
   NEXT Count
   OUTPUT Line
ENDPROCEDURE

FOR Row ← 1 TO 5
   CALL Stars(Row)
NEXT Row
questions.tip: Procedures are run with CALL in Cambridge pseudocode.

questions.q:
Write pseudocode that:
(a) inputs members' names until "END" is entered and writes each name to a new text file "Members.txt" [3]
(b) then reads the file back and outputs the number of names stored in it. [2]
(c) State the file mode that should be used to add more names later without deleting the existing ones. [1]
ms: (a) OPENFILE "Members.txt" FOR WRITE and CLOSEFILE after writing (1)
(a) loop that inputs names until "END" (END not written) (1)
(a) WRITEFILE "Members.txt", Name inside the loop (1)
(b) OPENFILE … FOR READ with a loop WHILE NOT EOF("Members.txt") (1)
(b) READFILE each line, increment a counter, output the count after the loop (1)
(c) APPEND (OPENFILE "Members.txt" FOR APPEND)
questions.model:
(a)
OPENFILE "Members.txt" FOR WRITE
OUTPUT "Enter a name, or END to finish"
INPUT Name
WHILE Name <> "END" DO
   WRITEFILE "Members.txt", Name
   INPUT Name
ENDWHILE
CLOSEFILE "Members.txt"
(b)
Count ← 0
OPENFILE "Members.txt" FOR READ
WHILE NOT EOF("Members.txt") DO
   READFILE "Members.txt", Name
   Count ← Count + 1
ENDWHILE
CLOSEFILE "Members.txt"
OUTPUT "Number of members: ", Count
(c) APPEND.
questions.tip: FOR WRITE creates a new file and overwrites anything already there.

questions.q:
The arrays Names[1:30] and Scores[1:30] store the names and test scores of 30 students; Names[1] belongs with Scores[1], and so on.
Write an algorithm in pseudocode that outputs:
• the name and score of the student with the highest score
• the number of students whose score is above the average (mean) score.
ms: initialises Total ← 0 and a variable to track the highest (e.g. HighIndex ← 1 or HighScore ← Scores[1]) (1)
loop through all 30 elements (1)
adds each score to Total (1)
compares each score with the current highest and updates it (1)
stores the index / name of the student with the highest score (1)
calculates Average ← Total / 30 after the first loop (1)
second loop counting scores greater than the average (1)
outputs the name, highest score and count with messages (1)
questions.model:
Total ← 0
HighIndex ← 1
FOR I ← 1 TO 30
   Total ← Total + Scores[I]
   IF Scores[I] > Scores[HighIndex]
      THEN
         HighIndex ← I
   ENDIF
NEXT I
Average ← Total / 30
AboveCount ← 0
FOR I ← 1 TO 30
   IF Scores[I] > Average
      THEN
         AboveCount ← AboveCount + 1
   ENDIF
NEXT I
OUTPUT "Highest: ", Names[HighIndex], " with ", Scores[HighIndex]
OUTPUT "Number above average: ", AboveCount
questions.tip: Storing the INDEX of the highest score lets you output the matching name from the parallel array.
